description: A wide 16:9 left-to-right pipeline diagram of how a language model answers one sentence. On the far LEFT a rounded speech box with the text 'How many city e-bike battery packs do we have in Manchester stores?' and above it a small grey label 'Emma asks'. To its right, one large rounded panel filled very light sky blue labelled 'The model' at its top left. Inside that panel, five rounded white boxes in a row joined by right-pointing arrows, each with a small number above it: '2' box 'Tokens' with grey caption 'text cut into pieces'; '3' box 'Vectors' with caption 'each piece becomes numbers'; '4' box 'Attention' with caption 'each piece looks back'; '5' box '24 blocks' with caption 'attention, then MLP, 24 times'; '6' box 'Probabilities' with caption 'one score per token, then a pick'. To the right of the panel, a rounded box labelled 'the next token' with a small number '7' above it. A thick curved arrow loops from 'the next token' back along the TOP of the panel to the 'Tokens' box, labelled '7 · add it, run again'. A thin rounded frame surrounds the whole flow with a small label at its top left '1 · The game: guess the next token'. BELOW the model panel, centered, a rounded box filled light green labelled 'Training' with caption 'where the numbers in the blocks come from' and a small number '8' above it, with an upward arrow into the '24 blocks' box. On the bottom RIGHT, a rounded box filled light ember orange labelled 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2' with caption 'Manchester stores: 5,400', with a small number '9' above it, and a dashed grey line between it and the model panel labelled 'no connection yet'. Labels as plain text, no brackets, spelled exactly as given, no other text.

A vertical architecture diagram of one transformer block, read from bottom to top, on a wide 16:9 canvas with the block in the center. At the BOTTOM a row of six small rounded tiles labelled 'vectors in, one per token, 896 numbers each'. An arrow goes up into a tall rounded panel filled very light sky blue labelled 'one block' at its top left. Inside the panel, from bottom to top: a thin white box 'normalise'; above it a wide white box with a sky-blue outline 'Attention' with grey caption 'each token mixes in earlier tokens'; above it a small circle with a plus sign; a thin line runs from below the first 'normalise' box, around the left side of the Attention box, into this plus circle, labelled 'add back the input'. Above the plus circle a thin white box 'normalise'; above it a wide white box with a green outline 'MLP' with grey caption 'each token on its own'; above it a second small circle with a plus sign, with a second bypass line around the left side of the MLP box labelled 'add back the input'. An arrow goes up out of the panel to a row of six small rounded tiles labelled 'vectors out, same size'. To the RIGHT of the panel, a tall curly bracket spanning the panel with the text 'repeat 24 times in Qwen2.5-0.5B'. Labels as plain text, no brackets, spelled exactly as given, no other text.

A wide 16:9 left-to-right timeline diagram of how a chat model is made. Three rounded stage boxes in a row joined by thick right-pointing arrows, each with a small number above it. Box '1' filled light sky blue: title 'Pretraining', grey caption lines 'guess the next token', 'on public text: web pages, books, code', '18 trillion tokens for Qwen2.5'. Box '2' white with a sky-blue outline: title 'Instruction tuning', caption lines 'example conversations', 'a request, then a good reply'. Box '3' white with a green outline: title 'Preference tuning', caption lines 'two replies to one request', 'learn from the one people prefer'. Under each box a small rounded grey chip saying what the model can now do: under 1 'continues documents', under 2 'answers requests', under 3 'answers the way people prefer'. To the right of box 3, a tall vertical dashed line labelled at its top 'last training day'. To the right of the line, a rounded box with a thick dark outline labelled 'Frozen weights' with caption 'using the model never changes them'. Labels as plain text, no brackets, spelled exactly as given, no other text.

A wide 16:9 concept diagram of why a language model makes up a stock number. On the LEFT a large rounded panel filled light sky blue labelled 'The model'. Inside it, two stacked white boxes: the upper one 'Weights' with grey caption 'patterns learnt from public text', the lower one 'The context' with grey caption 'system prompt and Emma's question'. From the right side of the panel, an arrow to a rounded white speech box with the text 'a plausible number'. On the far RIGHT a rounded box filled light ember orange labelled 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2' containing a small database cylinder with the text 'BAT-500 · Manchester · 5,400'. Between the model panel and the Ledgerline box, a dashed grey line broken in the middle, labelled 'no connection'. Along the BOTTOM, two rounded sockets with green outlines, side by side, each with an arrow pointing up into the lower box of the model panel: the left socket 'Knowledge' with caption 'put the facts into the context · Lecture 3'; the right socket 'Tools' with caption 'let it look them up in Ledgerline · Lecture 4'. Labels as plain text, no brackets, spelled exactly as given, no other text.
